implemented_requirements.evidence: config.py defines BEGINNER, INTERMEDIATE, EXPERT as Difficulty namedtuples and DIFFICULTY_LEVELS list; gui.py builds menu radio buttons from DIFFICULTY_LEVELS and creates Board with the selected difficulty.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player uncovers cells by clicking on them
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py binds left‑click (<Button-1>) on each button to _on_left_click which calls board.reveal_cell.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate how many mines are adjacent
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.Board calculates adjacent_mines; gui._refresh_board displays the number with appropriate color when cell.is_revealed and cell.adjacent_mines > 0.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Uncovering a mine causes the player to lose
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.reveal_cell returns "mine" when a revealed cell is a mine; gui._on_left_click calls board.reveal_all_mines and then _end_game(won=False).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board display updates after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: After every reveal or flag action gui calls _refresh_board which updates all button visuals according to the current Board state.
gui binds right‑click (<Button-3> and <Button-2>) to _on_right_click which calls board.toggle_flag; flagged state is stored in Cell.is_flagged.
In _refresh_board, flagged cells are rendered with text "🚩" and background FLAGGED_BG, different from unrevealed cells.

judge.summary: The provided source implements a fully functional Minesweeper game with three preset difficulties, click‑to‑reveal, adjacency numbers, loss on mine, live board updates, right‑click flagging and a unique flagged‑cell visual. The code is self‑contained, uses Tkinter for the UI, and appears ready to run, meeting all core benchmark requirements.
